_comment: Manually-maintained Australian Competition Tribunal appeal data, keyed by ACCC merger_id. Merged into the frontend data by scripts/static_data (see loaders.load_tribunal_appeals and enrichment.link_tribunal_appeals). IMPORTANT: an entry here does NOT by itself make a merger 'under appeal' — a matter stays listed after it finishes. A merger is shown as under appeal only while 'status' is 'current' (anything other than 'concluded' counts as current; a finished/withdrawn appeal must be marked 'concluded'). Fields: tribunal_number (e.g. 'ACT 1 of 2026'), tribunal_url (the tribunal matter page), appeal_type (one of party_denial / party_conditional_clearance / third_party_clearance — see scripts/constants/tribunal.py), appellant (who lodged the review), status ('current' | 'concluded'), filed_date, and documents[] which are folded into the merger's event timeline regardless of status. Once concluded, also set: outcome (one of affirmed / set_aside / varied / withdrawn / dismissed), effective_determination (the ACCC-style determination that now stands — same as the ACCC's when affirmed, the opposite when set aside, e.g. 'Approved' / 'Not approved' — used to render the status badge like 'Approved · on appeal'), and concluded_date. Each document: date, filed_by, description, confidentiality ('Confidential' | 'Non-confidential'), url (direct tribunal link, treated like an ACCC url), and optionally url_gh (local mirror served from data/raw/matters/{id}/). Tribunal scraping will maintain this file automatically in future; for now it is edited by hand.
